Muscles needed for crutch use in cauda equina lesion are the shoulder depressors and exten-
sors along with elbow extensors.

The lower fibers of trapezius depress the scapulae.

The latissimus dorsi assists in depression of the arm with the teres major and pectoralis major.
It adducts, extends, and internally rotates the shoulder.

Y (RE Question 150

A therapist is evaluating a patient who suffered brain injury in a motor vehicle accident. The
somatosensory cortex is involved, resulting in deficits in sensation in the right upper and
lower extremities. The therapist knows from visualizing the homunculus that at least part of
the injury is in one of the following locations:

1- Inferior right hemisphere of the somatosensory cortex.

2- Superior right hemisphere of the somatosensory cortex.

3- Inferior left hemisphere of the somatosensory cortex.

4- Superior left hemisphere of the somatosensory cortex.

Correct Answer: 4

rationale:

The right hemisphere is responsible for the left side of the body and vice versa and the presen-
tation of the human body in the primary somatosensory cortex is up-side-down which means
the Superior part receives sensations from the lower extremity, the middle part receives sen-
sations from the upper extremity and the inferior part receives sensations from the head.

Correct Answer: 4
rationale:

Neuromuscular System
Chapter 2
A physical therapist is ordered to evaluate a 65-year-old woman who has suffered a recent 
stroke. The occupational therapist informs the physical therapist that the patient has aprax­
ia. She cannot brush her teeth on command. However, she can point out the toothbrush and 
verbalize the purpose of the brush. From this information, what sort of apraxia does this 
patient have? How should the physical therapist approach treatment?
1- Ideomotor apraxia. The physical therapist should speak in short, concise sentences.
2- Ideomotor apraxia. The physical therapist should always give the patient 3 step commands.
3- Ideomotor apraxia. The physical therapist should always give the patient 5  step commands.
4- Ideational apraxia. The physical therapist should speak in short, concise sentences.
Question 245
A 60-year-old woman who has suffered a recent stroke has right-side homonymous hemi­
anopsia. Which of the following statements is true about placement of eating utensils in 
early rehabilitation?
1- The utensils should be placed on the left side of the plate.
2- The utensils should be placed on the right side of the plate.

PPTE Review & Study Guide
Rock-port 1 mile test used to test?
1- muscles
2- cardiovascular fitness
3- CNS
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
The Rockport walking test is an evaluation you can self-administer to determine your  cardiovas­
cular fitness , it evaluates the capacity of your lungs in relation to the volume of exercise you can 
tolerate. The aim of the test is to measure your VO2 max, the maximum amount of oxygen you 
can utilize during intense exercise, measured in milliliters of oxygen used per kilogram of body 
weight per minute (ml/kg/min)
What is the goal of the first phase of rehabilitation on Cardiopulmonary
1- help the patient to advance from passive range of motion ROM to active
2- increase endurance- Oxygen consumption
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
The goal of this first stage is to recuperate and allow your body to begin the healing process.  It 
begins by assessing the patient’s physical ability and motivation to tolerate rehabilitation. Ther­
apists and nurses may start by guiding patients through non-strenuous exercises in the bed or 
at the bedside, focusing on a range of motion and limiting hospital deconditioning and this help 
increasing endurance and oxygen consumption by capturing atmospheric oxygen and distribut­
ing it into the blood stream through diffusion.
Which of the following is the most appropriate trunk and head position, in degrees, to start 
chest physiotherapy?
1- 0
2-15
3- 30
4- 45
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
This position is best for draining the bottom front parts of your lungs , and enable gravity to assist 
the mobilization of secretions

At the beginning of the muscle activity which make increase of blood supply to it

Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
The diaphragm, located below the lungs, is the major muscle of respiration. It is a large, dome-
shaped muscle that contracts rhythmically and continually, and most of the time, involuntarily. 
Upon inhalation, diaphragm contracts and flattens and the chest cavity enlarges his movement 
creates a vacuum in your chest, allowing your chest to expand and pull in air . external intercos­
tal have fibres that are angled obliquely downward and forward from rib to rib. The contraction 
of these fibres raises each rib toward rib above, assisting in inhalation
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
intercostal muscles are a group of muscles found between the ribs which are responsible for 
helping form and maintain the cavity produced by the ribs.muscles assist with expansion and 
contraction during breathing and mainly involved in the mechanical aspect of breathing by help­
ing expand and shrink the size of the chest cavity
external intercostal have fibres that are angled obliquely downward and forward from rib to rib. 
The contraction of these fibres raises each rib toward the rib above, with the overall effect of 
raising the rib cage, assisting in inhalation but the role of internal intercostal is in forced expira­
tion , internal intercostals pull down on the rib cage and push air out of the lungs
Correct Answer: 2 : 2to 5 min. in excessive secretions 3-5 Min
rationale:
percussion is usually done for three to five minutes  to allow as much mucus as possible to drain 
from your lungs  and is sometimes followed by vibration over the same area for approximately 
15 seconds. The person is then encouraged to cough or huff forcefully to get the mucus out of 
the lungs

Question 14
Fracture Lower humerus fracture, therapist tend to do very gradual stretch:
1.	 to prevent disuse atrophy
2.	 to prevent hypertrophy
3.	 to stimulate muscle
4.	 to prevent muscle and tendon rupture.
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
exerting too much energy or going too deep into a stretch can result in a torn muscle. Slowly 
ease into your stretches. 
Question 15

the hummers with severe limitation of the ROM. The therapist needs to perform a very grad­
ual stretch to:
1.	 avoid disuse atrophy
2.	 avoid hypertrophy
3.	  prevent muscle and tendon tear
4.	  stimulate muscle
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
stretching a muscle slowly prevents it from overextending and being damaged. When stretches 
occur too quickly, such as with bouncing, the muscle can be seriously damaged

A patient presents to an outpatient physical therapy clinic with 140 degree kyphoscoliosis 
curve. What is the therapist’s greatest concern?

2.	 Gait deviation.
3.	 Pulmonary status.
4.	 Poor upright standing posture
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
kyphoscoliosis is a thoracic cage deformity that causes extrapulmonary restriction of the lungs 
and gives rise to impairment of pulmonary functions, as restrictive lung diseases. The condition 
may be primary (idiopathic) or secondary to neuromuscular disease, spondylitis ...
When O2 demand in heart decrease what happened ?
1.	 decrease HR multiplied by systolic pressure
2.	 decrease diastolic pressure
3.	  increase coronary arteries
4.	  increase HR multiplied by systolic pressure
Which of the following is the deconditioning effect on heart associated with bed rest?
1.	 decrease VO2 max .
2.	 Decrease heart rate .
3.	  Increase plasma volume .
4.	 Increase cardiac output .
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
By decreasing oxygen demand , the amount of blood that normally fills the ventricles decreases 
so diastolic blood pressure decrease
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
(VO2max) is reduced in individuals confined to bed rest,
To counteract this decrease in stroke volume and maintain sufficient cardiac output, a gradual 
increase in heart rate , Bed rest is also associated with an increase in sodium excretion and, as 
water tends to follow sodium, this leads to sodium diuresis that cause to the reduction in plasma 
volume

coronary artery supply heart during

Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
There are two primary coronary arteries, the right coronary artery (RCA) and the left main coro­
nary artery (LMCA). Both of these originate from the base of the aorta 
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
There are two coronary arteries,  each containing several branches: Right coronary artery and 
left coronary arteries , Both of these arteries originate from the root of the aorta, immediately 
above the aortic valve .the left coronary artery originates from the left aortic sinus, while the right 
coronary artery originates from the right aortic sinus
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Coronary blood flow occurs mostly during diastole because the coronary vasculature has one 
particular property: it is compressed by the contracting myocardium such that no flow occurs 
during systole , during systole, intramuscular blood vessels are compressed and twisted by the 
contracting heart muscle and blood flow to the left ventricle is at its lowest

Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Systems
Chapter 3
A patient asks the therapist to explain the function of his medication verapamil (a calcium an­
tagonist). Which of the following points should be conveyed in the therapist’s explanation?
1.	 Verapamil causes decreased contractility of the heart and vasodilation of the coronary 
arteries
2.	 Verapamil causes decreased contractility of the heart and vasoconstriction of the coronary ar­
teries
3.	 Verapamil causes increased contractility of the heart and vasodilation of the coronary arteries
4.	 Verapamil causes increased contractility of the heart and vasoconstriction of the coronary arter­
ies
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Un-modifiable risk factors (irreversible )
age, male sex, race, and family history.
Modifiable risk factors:  
smoking, exposure to second-hand smoke, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, high cholesterol (total 
or LDL-C) levels,( low HDL-C) levels, high triglyceride levels, diabetes, abdominal obesity, sed­
entary lifestyle, high homocysteine levels, and high levels of C-reactive protein (which indicates 
inflammation).
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Calcium plays a central role in the electrical stimulation of cardiac cells and in the mechani­
cal contraction of smooth muscle cells in the walls of arteries. Calcium-channel blockers are 
relatively new synthetic drugs that work by blocking the passage of calcium into the muscle 
cells that control the size of blood vessels, thereby preventing the muscles of the arteries from 
constricting so decrease heart rate and contractility, which leads to a reduction in myocardial 
oxygen demand, which makes them excellent antianginal drugs

seventh, and eighth thoracic vertebrae by the esophagus, aorta, and thoracic duct

1.	 sympathetic
2.	 parasympathetic

The patient is referred by a physician to begin outpatient cardiac rehabilitation. Which of the 
following is not a contraindication to enter an outpatient program?
1.	 Resting systolic blood pressure of 210 mmHg
2.	 Third-degree atrioventricular block
3.	 Resting ST displacement less than 1 mm.
4.	 Acute fever
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is usually caused by changes in genes (gene mutations) that 
cause the heart muscle to thicken. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy typically affects the muscular 
wall (septum) between the two bottom chambers of the heart (ventricles). The thickened wall 
might block blood flow out of the heart
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
the heart is innervated by sympathetic and parasympathetic fibres from the autonomic  branch 
of the peripheral nervous system. The network of nerves supplying the heart is called the cardi­
ac plexus. It receives contributions from the right and left vagus nerves,as well as contributions 
from the sympathetic trunk

PPTE Review & Study Guide
A physician orders stage II cardiac rehabilitation for a patient. The orders are to exercise the 
patient below 7 metabolic equivalents (METS). Which of the following is a contraindicated 
activity?
1.	 Riding a stationary bike at approximately 5.5 mph
2.	 Descending a flight of stairs independently
3.	 Ironing
4.	 Ambulate independently at 5-6 mph
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
metabolic equivalent for task (MET) is a unit that estimates the amount of energy used by the 
body during physical activity, as compared to resting metabolism. The unit is standardized so it 
can apply to people of varying body weight and compare different activities
one MET is defined as 3.5 mL O2 uptake/kg per min, which is the resting oxygen uptake in a 
sitting position). Less than 5 METS is poor, 5–8 METS is fair, 9–11 METS is good, and 12 METS 
or more is excellent
main character at cardiac patient :
1.	 bluish limbs
2.	 pain at the calf
3.	 edema of limbs 
4.	 abdominal breathing
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
cardiac edema occurs when the heart’s diseased or overworked left ventricle (heart’s lower 
chamber) isn’t able to pump out enough of the blood it receives from your lungs. 
Question 65
Question 64
Which make rapid decrease in heart rate ?
1.	 preganglionic fiber
2.	  postganglionic fiber
3.	 fiber near to heart      
Question66
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Heart rate is an important physiologic regulator of total cardiac output. Through strong influenc­
es of the autonomic nervous system, the heart rates in a newborn can range from 70 to 220 
beats/min and profoundly impact cardiac output.Fibers from the autonomic divisions alter the 
intrinsic heart rate by changing the course of spontaneous diastolic depolarization on pacemak­
er cells in the SA node. Activation of the cardiac sympathetic fibers will increase the heart rate, 
whereas stimulation of cardiac parasympathetic fibers will decrease the heart rate.

Patient after exercise experienced low heart rate, low blood pressure, headedness, his skin 
is pale and cold. What is the most likely?
1.	 Angina
2.	 cardiogenic shock
3.	  myocardial infarction.
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
if a current from outside the body passes through the heart, it can mask these impulses and 
disturb the heart’s rhythm. This irregular heartbeat is called arrhythmia and can even manifest

Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
 lack of visible P waves preceding QRS complexes suggests a lack of sinus beats; this may 
occur with sinus dysfunction or in the presence of fibrillation or flutter waves
Correct Answer: 2    cardiogenic shock because skin is pale
rationale: cardiogenic shock, also known as cardiac shock, happens when your heart cannot 
pump enough blood and oxygen to the brain and other vital organs. This is a life-threatening 
emergency. It is treatable if diagnosed right away, so it’s important to know the warning signs , 
pressure, fullness or a squeezing pain in the center of your chest that lasts for more than a few 
minutes. Pain spreading to your shoulder, one or both of your arms, your back, or even your 
teeth and jaw , pale skin . Shortness of breath

PPTE Review & Study Guide
A 50-year-old man has a persistent cough, purulent sputum, abnormal dilation of bronchi, 
more frequent involvement of the left lower lobe than the right, hemoptysis, and reduced 
forced vital capacity.  What is the most likely pulmonary dysfunction?
1.	 Chronic bronchitis
2.	 Emphysema
3.	 Asthma
4.	 Bronchiectasis
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
first-degree atrioventricular (AV) block is a condition of abnormally slow conduction through the 
AV node. It is defined by ECG changes that include a PR interval of greater than 0.20 without 
disruption of atrial to ventricular conduction. This condition is generally asymptomatic and dis­
covered only on routine ECG
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
bronchiectasis is a long-term condition where the airways of the lungs become widened, leading 
to a build-up of excess mucus that can make the lungs more vulnerable to infection. The most 
common symptoms of bronchiectasis include: a persistent cough that usually brings up phlegm 
(sputum) shortness of breath

Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Systems
Chapter 3
A patient with restrictive lung disease secondary to circumferential thoracic burns demon­
strate decreased ability to expand the lower rib cage and push the abdominal wall anteriorly. 
In this case, the therapist should consider the use of facilitation techniques to enhance the 
function of the:
1.	 rectus abdominis
2.	 anterior scalenus
3.	 internal intercostals
4.	 diaphragm
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
rales or crackles are respiratory sounds often heard in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease 
(COPD) as well as in restrictive conditions, such as heart failure, lung fibrosis and pneumonia. 
1 Forgacs proposed that crackles heard during inspiration were related to sudden opening air­
ways 
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Diaphragm breathing used for restrictive pulmonary disease because its action is in conjunction 
with the intercostal muscles, it lowers the pressure in the thoracic cavity. This enables air to 
enter the lungs. When breathing out, the diaphragm relaxes along with the intercostal muscles, 
allowing air to leave. Air may be forced out faster by increasing abdominal pressure using the 
transverse abdominis muscle.
Which of the following is the most appropriate description of the expiratory flow rate in 
chronic obstructive pulmonary disease?
1.	 Variable
2.	 Increase
3.	 Decrease
4.	 Unchanged
You are evaluating a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. You would not ex­
pect to find:
1.	 the presence of hypercapnia
2.	 increased total lung capacity
3.	 increased vital capacity
4.	 abnormal ventilation/perfusion ratio
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exhibit increases in lung volume 
due to expiratory airflow limitation. Increases in lung volumes may affect upper airway patency 
and compensatory responses to inspiratory flow limitation (IFL) during sleep

PPTE Review & Study Guide
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
The sinoatrial node ( SA node or sinus node) is a group of cells known as pacemaker cells, lo­
cated in the wall of the right atrium of the heart.
Conduction pathway  :starts when your sinoatrial (SA) node creates an excitation signal.
The excitation signal travels to: Your atria (top heart chambers), telling them to contract.
-The atrioventricular (AV) node, delaying the signal until your atria are empty of blood.
-The bundle of His (center bundle of nerve fibers), carrying the signal to the Purkinje fibers.
-The Purkinje fibers to your ventricles (bottom heart chambers), causing them to contract

Question 106
Question 107
when detect target heart rate in unstable angina we don`t make
1.	 valsalva maneuver
2.	 isometric ex
3.	 heavy arm ex
4.	 isotonic ex  
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Isometric exercise is defined as a muscular contraction without movement (eg, handgrip) and 
imposes greater pressure than volume load on the left ventricle in relation to the body’s ability 
to supply oxygen. Cardiac output is not increased as much as in isotonic exercise because 
increased resistance in active muscle groups limits blood flow. Resistance exercise combines 
both isometric and isotonic exercise (such as free weight lifting). 
Performing the Valsalva maneuver causes an increase in intrathoracic pressure, leading to a 
reduction in preload to the heart
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Performing isometric exercises places too much load on the left ventricle of the heart for many 
cardiac patients

Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Systems
Chapter 3
Which of the following minutes of running are most commonly required in a cardiovascular 
fitness field test?
1.	 10
2.	 12
3.	 14
4.	 16
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Cardio fitness measures how well your body can perform a rhythmic, dynamic activity at a mod­
erate to high intensity for extended periods of time.
There are :Treadmill tests ,The three-minute step test and The Rockport walk test .
The 12-minute run/walk test measures how far a person can cover (run, walk, jog) in 12 minutes. 
Ideally you want to take this test on a standard running track, or a location where you can mea­
sure distance run without having to stop.

Question 109
A therapist is ordered by a physician to treat a patient with congestive heart failure in an out­
patient cardiac rehabilitation facility. Which of the following signs and symptoms should the 
therapist not expect?
1.	 Stenosis of the mitral valve
2.	 Orthopnea
3.	 Decreased preload of the right heart
4.	 Pulmonary edema
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
preload is defined as the stretch of myocardium or end-diastolic volume of the ventricles and 
most frequently refers to the volume in a ventricle just before the start of systole.
-In heart failure, there is a compensatory increase in blood volume that serves to increase ven­
tricular preload and thereby enhance stroke volume by the Frank-Starling mechanism.
-Preload increases with exercise (slightly).

most frequently refers to the volume in a ventricle just before the start of systole.

-In heart failure, there is a compensatory increase in blood volume that serves to increase ven-
tricular preload and thereby enhance stroke volume by the Frank-Starling mechanism.
-Preload increases with exercise (slightly).

rationale:
•

•	
 In people with emphysema, the air sacs in the lungs (alveoli) are damaged. Over time, the

small ones.
•

Question 117
Question 116
Question 115
Correct Answer: 5
rationale:
The first sound of heart (lub) corresponds with the closing of the AV valves ( mitral and tricuspid 
valves). The second sound  (dup) corresponds to closing of the semilunar valves (aortic and pul­
monic valves). Therefore, the first sound is indicative of the onset of ventricular systole, and the 
second sound is indicative of the onset of ventricular diastole. The first sound is usually lower in 
pitch and longer than the second.

Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Systems
Chapter 3
patient with emphysema and has barrel chest which statement document it
1.	 depressed ribs angel
2.	 increase transverse diameter    
3.	 decrease ant post diameter
4.	 increase intercostal space   
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
In a barrel-shaped chest, the anteroposterior diameter is equal to or greater than its lateral(trans­
verse) diameter . The ribs become more horizontal and dorsal kyphosis is present in the majority 
of cases. Other findings are prominent sternum, elevated clavicles, shortened neck, and wid­
ened intercostal spaces. Barrel-shaped chest is usually seen in advanced emphysema. Aging 
can also produce barrel-shaped deformity of the chest without any lung diseased.
All of the following conditions are obstructive lung disorder except:
1.	 chronic bronchitis
2.	 pneumonia
3.	 emphysema
4.	 cystic fibrosis
A 45-year-old woman with bronchiectasis is referred for chest
physiotherapy. She has reduced breath sounds on the right lower chest with crepitus. Which 
of the following is the main reason to accurately identify the area involved, before the start 
of the session?
1.	 Better results
2.	 Secretions removal
3.	 Teaching technique
4.	 Prevention of disease spreading to other Areas
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Obstructive lung diseases are  are characterized by an  obstruction,inflammation and narrrowing 
in the air passages, with slow and shallow exhalation:Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease 
(COPD),chronic bronchitis,brochiolitis,Asthma,Bronchhiectasis,cystic fibrosis.
Restrictive conditions are defined by difficulty filling the lungs with air during inhalation. 
Intrinsic restrictive disorders are those that occur due to restriction in the lungs (often a “stiffen­
ing”) and include: pneumonia,Pneumoconioses,Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) 
and Sarcoidosis 
Extrinsic restrictive disorders refer to those that originate outside of the lungs. These include 
impairment caused by:pleural effusion,pneumothorax and pleuristy.

Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Pulmonary ventilation is commonly referred to as breathing. It is the process of air flowing into 
the lungs during inspiration (inhalation) and out of the lungs during expiration (exhalation). Air

 Which of the following is a common reason for breathlessness occurring in scoliosis pa­

Which of the following is the most suitable for airway management?
1.	 Jaw lift
2.	  Chin lift 
3.	 Jaw thrust
4.	 Modified jaw thrust
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
While most people with scoliosis have a mild form of the disorder, scoliosis may sometimes 
cause complications, including: Breathing problems. In severe scoliosis, the rib cage may press 
against the lungs, making it more difficult to breathe.
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
DLCO (“Diffusing Capacity of the Lungs Test” ):
Pulmonary diffusing capacity for oxygen increases progressively with increasing severity of ex­
ercise; it exceeds the  at high levels of exercise by amounts greater than can be accounted for 
by the difference in diffusivity of the test gases.
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Airway management is the  required to maintain or restore an individual’s ventilation to lungs 
from mouth and nose. The head-tilt/chin-lift and jaw-thrust are also basic airway management 
maneuvers. By preventing the tongue from obstructing the upper airway, these maneuvers are 
used to avoid airway obstruction in unconscious individuals. The head-tilt/chin-lift is not recom­
mended in individuals for which cervical spine injury, or the injury of the upper spine in the neck, 
is a concern. On the other hand, the jaw-thrust maneuver is suitable when cervical spine injury 
is suspected. Obese patients need more head elevation than typical when we open the airway.

discomfort associated with pregnancy-induced varicose veins?

Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is a condition where plaque builds up in the arteries that carry 
blood to areas like your legs, arms, and internal organs.Damage of the artries is due to High 
BP,High cholestrol,DM and smoking.If you have PAD, you may experience intermittent clau­
dication ( The most characteristic symptom of PAD is claudication which is a pain in the lower 
extremity muscles brought on by walking and relieved with rest)., or pain when you walk or 
climb stairs that goes away with rest. This is because your muscles aren’t getting enough blood. 
This is due to blood vessels that have become narrowed or blocked. Other symptoms of PAD 
include: blue or pale skin ,weak pulse in legs or feet and slow wound healing. 
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Non-pharmacological interventions including include avoidance of prolonged standing and 
straining, external compression devices (e.g. bandages, support stockings, intermittent pneu­
matic compression devices) and leg elevation can provide relief from discomfort and may im­
prove symptoms in some women

Arteriosclerosis is: 
1.	 A condition in which an artery wall thickens 
2.	 A condition in which a vein wall thickens 
3.	 Hardening (and loss of elasticity) of medium or large arteries     
4.	 Hardening (and loss of elasticity) of medium or large veins
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
If you have Raynaud’s Disease (i.e. your hands change colour from white to blue to red) do not 
use Ice cube massage.
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
•	
Arteriosclerosis is a broader term for the condition in which the arteries narrow and harden, 
leading to poor circulation of blood throughout the body . Atherosclerosis is a specific type of 
arteriosclerosis. Atherosclerosis is thickening of the walls of the arteries.
•	
Arteriolosclerosis means hardening of the arterioles, which are small arteries. It affects pri­
marily the inner and middle layers of the walls of arterioles. 
•	
Atherosclerosis affects medium-sized and large arteries, and is the primary cause of heart 
disease and stroke. Atherosclerosis begins when damage occurs to the inner layer (intima) 
of your artery wall. 
Which of the following scientific terms is defined as chronic inflammation of the innermost 
layer of the arteries?
1.	 Aneurysm
2.	 Angina pectoris
3.	 Atherosclerosis
4.	 Deep arterial thrombosis

2.	 brachial artery 15 sec*4
3.	 radial artery 30 sec * 2
4.	 carotid artery 60 se
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Atherosclerosis begins when damage occurs to the inner layer of your artery wall. This layer is 
called the intima. The surface of your intima is lined with endothelial cells. This thin lining, called 
the endothelium, is the barrier between your blood and your artery wall.

Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Systems
Chapter 3
The most common type of stroke is and its primary precipitating factor is
1.	 Atherothrombotic, atherosclerosis
2.	 Atherothrombotic, hypertension
3.	 Hemorrhage, atherosclerosis
4.	 Hemorrhage, hypertension
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
•	
Atherothrombotic stroke is the most common. It occurs when a blood clot forms on an ath­
erosclerotic plaque within a blood vessel in the brain and blocks blood flow
•	
Most ischemic strokes are caused by atherosclerosis, which is also called hardening of the 
arteries.  Over time, this can completely block blood flow.
•	
Blood vessels damaged by high blood pressure can narrow, rupture or leak. High blood 
pressure can also cause blood clots to form in the arteries leading to the brain, blocking

The most common type of stroke is and its primary precipitating factor is

rationale:

¢ Atherothrombotic stroke is the most common. It occurs when a blood clot forms on an ath-

* Most ischemic strokes are caused by atherosclerosis, which is also called hardening of the
arteries. Over time, this can completely block blood flow.

¢ Blood vessels damaged by high blood pressure can narrow, rupture or leak. High blood
pressure can also cause blood clots to form in the arteries leading to the brain, blocking

Cerebral embolism begin first from
1.	 heart
2.	 lung
3.	 vessels of lower limb
Pulmonary embolism begin first from
1.	 heart
2.	 lung
3.	 vessels of lower limb
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Blood clots that lead to embolic stroke can form anywhere. They usually come from the heart 
or arteries of the upper chest and neck. After breaking free, the clot travels through the blood­
stream to the brain. When it enters a blood vessel that’s too small to allow it to pass, the clot 
becomes stuck in place.
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
DVT is the most common cause of a pulmonary embolism. Other less frequent sources of pul­
monary embolism are a fat embolus (often linked to the breaking of a large bone), amniotic fluid 
embolus, air bubbles, and a deep vein thrombosis in the upper body.
in thrombosis we do
1.	 fat embolism
2.	 pulmonary embolism
3.	 arterial embolism
4.	 fracture embolism
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
DVT is the most common cause of a pulmonary embolism.A pulmonary embolism occurs when 
a part of the clot breaks off and travels to the lungs, a potential life threat

Basic Airway Management (Manual / Non equipment) all the following EXEPT:
1.	 head tilt

4.	 laryngeal mask airway (LMA)

rationale:

Advanced airway management involves the use of specialized medical equipment  The most 
commonly used device is the laryngeal mask airway (LMA) that is used as a temporary method 
to maintain an open airway during administration of anesthesia or as an immediate life-saving 
measure in a difficult airway situation

Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Systems
Chapter 3
Which statement incorrect about prevention of D.V.T:
1.	 use elastic stocking
2.	 abdominal binder
3.	 put patient with head elevated
Question 174
Which of the following measures/procedures are not of clinical importance for D.V.T patients 
1.	 Frequent turning 
2.	 Raising head above the level of the body  
3.	 Wearing compressive socks 
4.	 Passive range of motion exercises
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
-Compression stockings are thought to reduce the risk of DVT by exerting graduated pressure 
on the leg, with the pressure being greatest at the ankle. This, when combined with muscular 
activity in the limb, is thought to displace blood from the superficial venous system to the deep 
venous system.
-Prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis after major abdominal surgery. Abdominal binder is used 
helps to reduce postoperative pain, distress, and hemorrhage after surgeries .So, in theory, ab­
dominal binders may actually decrease DVT risk because they may help increase mobility after 
surgery.
Question 175
Question 176
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Compression stockings are thought to reduce the risk of DVT by exerting graduated pressure 
on the leg, with the pressure being greatest at the ankle. This, when combined with muscular 
activity in the limb, is thought to displace blood from the superficial venous system to the deep 
venous system..
PWhich of the following is NOT considered a strong risk factor for DVT?
1.	 Bed rest lasting longer than 3 days.
2.	 Hip/knee replacement.
3.	 MI within the last 3 months.
4.	 Major Trauma/lower limb fracture.
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Notes: Bed rest lasting longer than 3 days is NOT a strong risk factor, it is a WEAK risk factor.
Immboiltiy and prolonged bed rest is a risk factor of DVT.
One of the risks of hip replacement or knee replacement surgery is deep vein thrombosis (DVT).
MI was significantly associated with VTE (venous thromboembolism) but not after adjusting for 
VTE risk factors.
DVT of lower limb veins is one of the most common complications following surgeries for lower 
limb.

Pneumothorax - is an accumulation of air or gas in the pleural space (the space between viscer­
al and parietal pleura of the chest cavity).  It can happen secondary to trauma (traumatic pneu­
mothorax). When mediastinal shifts accompany it, it is called a tension pneumothorax. Pneumo­
thorax is the most frequently reported cause of tracheal deviation from pressure buildup.
Symptoms:
-Sharp, stabbing chest pain that worsens when trying to breath in.
-Shortness of breath.
-Bluish skin caused by a lack of oxygen.
-Fatigue.
-Rapid breathing and heartbeat.
-A dry, hacking cough.

4. be unable to understand speech

Correct Answer: 2

rationale:

The somatosensory cortex is a region of the brain which is responsible for receiving and pro-
cessing sensory information from across the body, such as touch, temperature, and pain. Symp-
toms that may be experienced as a result of damage:Numbness, Inability to Localize Sensations
,Inability to Judge Weight and Pressure and Phantom Limb Pain is experinced with amputess
and there is changes in somatosensory cortex.

« Question 185

pseudo claudication is due to compression of:
1. Femoral artery

2. Femoral nerve.

3. Cauda Equina.

4. Popliteal artery

Correct Answer: 3

rationale:

Pseudoclaudication” Syndrome Produced by Compression of the Cauda Equina.

Pain in the lower extremities associated with occlusive arterial disease is a common occurrence.
On relatively rare occasions, pain in the legs, precipitated by walking, is caused by compression
of the cauda equina by hypertrophic ridging or by a herniated lumbar disk.

Raynaud’s phenomenon is classically described with a triphasic color change of the digits with

Congestive Heart Failure is referred to the Physical Therapy Department for gait training. 
Which assessment test is the most reliable to calculate exercise capacity
1.	 Chair-stand
2.	 6-minute walk
3.	 Time up and go
4.	 Physical performance
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Exercise capacity can be assessed by the following tests :Maximal test (exercise stress test; 
EST),Cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET),Submaximal test (six-minute walk test; 6MWT),­
Submaximal treadmill test and Incremental shuttle walk test (ISWT).
The six-minute walk test (6MWT is a self-paced walking test well suited to a hospital or commu­
nity setting.
For patients with more severe classes of heart disease, 6MWT results correlate well with VO2 
peak, and only one 6MWT is recommended.
In addition to measuring exercise capacity, more specific functional testing can be used. Some 
examples such as Timed up and go test. More recently, combined measures such as the Short 
Physical Performance Battery (standing balance, walking speed, and chair stand) and the Func­
tional Difficulty Questionnaire have been validated in cardiac surgery patients.

Question 48

1- mother malnutrition
2- idiopathic
Question 49
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
This is due to its correlation with the TLR (Tonic Labyrinthine Reflex) - as an infant begins to 
integrate the TLR, the STNR emerges to help progress to the next phase of development, 
crawling. The symmetric tonic neck reflex is commonly referred to as the “crawling reflex” be­
cause it allows your baby to make the transition from laying down to getting up on their hands 
and knees.
- When your baby has reached the STNR stage, you may notice that when their neck and arms 
straighten, the legs will bend. When the neck and arms bend, the legs will straighten. These 
movements are important for crawling and taking their first steps.

physician describing?
1- Comminuted
2- Avulsion
3- Greenstick
4- Segmental
Question 57
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Greenstick fractures result from the bending of a bone. Any force that bends a long bone, 
such as an arm or leg bone, without fully breaking it can cause a greenstick fracture. Instead 
of snapping into two pieces, the bone cracks on one side ,is most common in young children.

Correct Answer: 3

Question 79
A child with spastic diplegia is now independent in using a walker. Additional goals desired 
by the physical therapist include increasing the child’s energy-efficiency and velocity while 
ambulating. In this case, the selection of walker that is most likely to help improve these 
factors is:
1- a standard anterior walker with no wheels.
2- an anterior rollator walker with two wheels.
3- a posterior rollator walker with two wheels.
4- a posterior rollator walker with four wheels.
Question 80
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
The benefits of the posterior rollator walker with four wheels: 
	
1. Facilitate more upright posture.
	
2. Decrease hip and trunk flexion during the stance phase.
	
3. Decrease double stance time.
	
4. Increase walking velocity.
	
5. Increase stability and interaction with the other children.
	
6. Decrease energy expenditure than anterior walker. 
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Start with rollator walker and progress to crutches. An independent gait is possible for some, 
usually with gluteus medius lurch and lumber lordosis. 
A 6 year-old child with myelomeningocele at the L5 level and minimal complications should 
be expected to ambulate with:
1- a reciprocating gait orthosis with a Rollator walker.
2- a shoe insert to maintain proper foot alignment and no ambulatory aid.
3- a knee-ankle-foot orthosis with crutches.
4- an ankle foot orthosis with crutches or a Rollator walker.

PPTE Review & Study Guide
A 50-year-old patient presents with hot flushes irritability, joint pain and lack of sleep. Which 
of the following is the most appropriate management?
1- Vitamins
2- Hysterectomy
3- Hormone replacement therapy
4- Oestrogen-progesterone preparation
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
As hormone replacement therapy is medication that contains female hormones, you take the 
medication to replace the estrogen that your body stops making during manopause . Hormone 
replacement therapy is most often used to treat Common manoposud symptoms including het 
plashes and vaginal discomfort and joint pain.
Question 11
Rickets is due to deficiency of vitamin:
1- C
2- B
3- K
4- D
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Vitamin D helps your child’s body absorb calcium and phosphorus from food. Not enough 
vitamin D makes it difficult. To maintain proper calcium and phosphorus levels in bone which 
can cause rickets.
Question 12
Which of the following is the minimum separation, in cm, of the rectus abdominis muscles 
in pregnancy that is considered clinically significant?
1- 1 Cm
2- 2 Cm
3- 3 Cm
4- 4 Cm
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
rectus muscles are normally fused at the midline with no more than 1 to 2 cm separating them 
(1). Rectus diastasis (RD) (diastasis recti, divarication of the rectus muscles) is an acquired 
condition in which the rectus muscles are separated by an abnormal distance along their 
length, but with no fascial defect.

to the linea alba cause it to stretch resulting in a widening of the interrectus distance. Most 
studies have agreed that the minimum interrectus distance to designate a diastasis is 2 cm. 
6 Diastasis recti is most common following pregnancy; however, obesity and prior abdominal 
operations can also be the cause.

Therapeutic Modalities - Therapeutic Exercises 
Chapter 5
Patient walking on slippery surface we teach him to do:
1- COG keeping close to the body
2- Wide base of support
3- Walking fast
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
The closer the body’s center of gravity is to its base of support, the more stable it is.
Question 1
the convex-concave role of the knee joint in open chain movement 
1-Tibia roll and glide on the femur in the same direction.
2-Tibia roll and glide on the femur in a different direction. 
3-Femur roll and glide on the tibia in the same direction. 
4-Femur rolls and glides on the tibia in a different direction.
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
choose it in closed chain
According to the convex /concave rule, the tibia is concave, and the femur is convex during the 
movement when the convex surface moves the gliding occurs opposite when the concave sur­
face moves the gliding movement occurs in the same direction. Also, the open chain means 
that the distal part isn’t touching the floor and that is why it is named opened.
Question 2
Which of the following is associated with the property to assume a greater
length than the pre-stretch state?
1- Elasticity
2- Plasticity
3- Flexibility
4- Extensibility
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Flexibility is the ability of a joint or series of joints to move through an unrestricted, pain-free 
range of motion. Stretching exercises are typically performed to increase flexibility and to al­
low an improved joint range of motion. Decreased flexibility may also lead to abnormal stress 
on structures and tissues distant from the initial site of inflexibility, elasticity is the ability of a 
deformed material body to return to its original shape and size when the forces causing the 
deformation are removed, and plasticity is s the ability of the tissue to undergo permanent de­
formation to substitute another defect. Tissue extensibility relates to tissue flexibility, which is 
related to the strength and power that your muscles can generate.

PPTE Review & Study Guide
All true of the following is true about passive movement except:
1- moving parts should be grasped gently.
2- unmoving parts should be supported.
3- sequence proximal to distal as it is promoting venous return.
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
The passive movement is done from distal to proximal to maintain Venus return and lymph 
flow.
Question 4
which statement is incorrect about the passive movement to
1- passive movement segment must hold gently.
2- proximal part must be supported.
3- passive movement from proximal to distal to increase lymph and venous return.
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
The passive movement the therapist does it from distal to proximal to improve venous and 
lymphatic flow and it is the same direction of fascia fibers.
Question 5
Which of the following is most commonly associated with a systematic
exercise plan planned performance of bodily movements, postures, and
physical activities?
1- Flexibility
2- Endurance
3- Therapeutic
4- Coordination
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Therapeutic exercises are movements and physical activities designed to restore function and 
flexibility, improve strength and decrease pain. If you are receiving physical therapy for an 
injury or a chronic condition, your physical therapist may incorporate therapeutic exercises in 
your treatment plan. Specific exercises like flexibility, endurance, and coordination were used.

Correct Answer: 3

Accessory Movements Definition - Movements within the joint and surrounding tissues that 
are necessary for normal range of motion that cannot be performed actively by the patient -

Type of contraction in which muscle lengthening to provide tension
1- eccentric cont

3- isotonic cont
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:

- Concentric contraction which MS shortening to provide tension.
- Isotonic contraction include both concentric and eccentric contraction.
Question 8
Joint play ROM which occurs not named with:
1- necessary to completion of joints ROM.
2- Passively occur.
3- under voluntary control.
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
joint play: small movements within a synovial joint that are independent of voluntary muscle 
contraction. These movements measure not more than 1/8 inch in any plane and follow the 
contour of the opposing joint surfaces. By nature, joint play is an involuntary movement that is 
inherent to the musculoskeletal system and cannot be introduced by voluntary muscles. A joint 
play is another name for the accessory movement.
Question 9
During underwater exercises which will be difficult
1- moving the limb horizontally.
2- moving the limb toward the bottom (against the bouncy force of water).
3- moving the limb to the surface.
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Buoyancy is an upward force exerted by a fluid in a direction opposite to a downward force 
such as gravity and thus it counters (partially or fully) the weight of an object immersed in the 
fluid. Moving the limb to the surface was used in active assisted training while moving horizon­
tally was used to work in gravity eliminated position.

334
PPTE Review & Study Guide
A 20-year-old athlete man sustained an injury to his quadriceps during a jump, Which of the 
following is the most appropriate preventative exercise program?
1- Aerobic
2- Static stretching
3- Ballistic stretching
4- Dynamic stretching
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Aerobic exercises reduce the risk of many conditions. It can reduce pain and improve function 
in people with arthritis. 
Aerobic exercise keeps your muscles strong, which can help you maintain mobility as you get 
older. Exercise can also lower the risk of falls and injuries from falls in older adults. And it can 
improve your quality of life. Ballistic exercise is a high-impact exercise that increases the rele­
vance of injury. Stretching is not preventive exercise even static stretching is possible for such 
a scenario, but it is not optimal.
Question 11
Which of the following types of stretching is associated with repeated
movements and momentum to gain desired range of motion?
1- Static
2- Ballistic
3- Dynamic
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Ballistic stretching is a form of stretching that uses body momentum from bouncing to force 
the body’s joints to move with a larger ROM than normal In ballistic stretching, the movement 
is done using a bouncing motion to force the joint to close more. Static stretching is the safest 
type of stretching and include applying stretch of constant intensity and velocity.
Question 12
If muscles co contract in equal force. Co-contraction of the biceps brachii and the triceps 
will result in what type of movement:
1- flexion
2- extension
3- isometric
4- supination
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
- co-contraction is a form of isometric exercise that specifically focuses on contracting muscles 
on the opposite side of joints against each other to stabilize the joint/hold position.
- In flexion bicepse will contract more than tricepse and the opposite will happen in extension.

335
Therapeutic Modalities - Therapeutic Exercises 
Chapter 5
What is the best way to first exercise the postural (or extensor) musculature when it is ex­
tremely weak to facilitate muscle control?
1- Isometrically
2- Concentrically
3- Eccentrically
4- Isokinetically
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
isometric exercises are static strength training workouts, these exercises provide muscular 
strength only in particular muscles as performed without moving the surrounding joints.
These workouts are done in only one position, and thus, they improve strength in only one 
position. They aim to improve your body’s stabilization to a great extent and help contract a 
particular muscle.
- Concentric exercise include exercise that shortens the muscle. 
- Eccentric exercise include exercise that lengthen the muscle .
- Isokinetic exercise include exercise that have constant velocity.
Question 14
A 65 - year - old man with Congestive Heart Failure is referred to the Physical Therapy De­
partment for gait training.
Which assessment test is the most reliable to calculate exercise capacity?
1- Chair - stand 
2- 6 - minute walk 
3- Time up and go 
4- Physical performance OD
5- Heart rate
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
- Exercise capacity can be assessed by the following tests: Maximal test (exercise stress test; 
EST), Cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET),Submaximal test (six-minute walk test; 6MWT),­
Submaximal treadmill test and Incremental shuttle walk test (ISWT).
- The six-minute walk test (6MWT is a self-paced walking test well suited to a hospital or com­
munity setting.
- For patients with more severe classes of heart disease, 6MWT results correlate well with 
VO2 peak, and only one 6MWT is recommended.
In addition to measuring exercise capacity, more specific functional testing can be used. Some 
examples such as Timed up and go test. More recently, combined measures such as the Short 
Physical Performance Battery (standing balance, walking speed, and chair stand) and the 
Functional Difficulty Questionnaire have been validated in cardiac surgery patients.
- Heart rate is not an option when dealing with patients that take medications to control their 
heart rate and of course patient with congestive heart failure should take heart rate regulators.

heart rate and of course patient with congestive heart failure should take heart rate regulators.

What is the type of contraction at the elbow flexion muscles?
 1- Isometric
 2- Eccentric
 3- Isokinetic
 4- Concentric
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
isometric contraction is a muscle contraction without motion. Isometric contractions are used 
to stabilize a joint, such as when a weight is held at waist level neither raising nor lowering it.
- Concentric exercise include exercise that shortens the muscle. 
- Eccentric exercise include exercise that lengthen the muscle .
- Isokinetic exercise include exercise that have constant velocity.
Question 16
Which of the following is the general recommendation regarding exercise
for normal older adults?
1- Low intensity
2- High intensity
3- Extreme intensity
4- Moderate intensity
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Moderate exercise doesn’t need to be athletic or difficult. Studies have shown that simply 
walking at a brisk pace for 30 minutes or more on most days can lead to significant health 
improvements. Add simple strengthening exercises two or three times a week and the benefits 
are even greater.
- Vigorous exercises are not recommended for older adults.

Chapter 5
Correct Answer: 4

A67 y female has acute sever RH.ARTHRITIS Physiotherapy in future do strengthening ex 
which one is better
1- isometric ex
2- isotonic ex
3- iso kinetic ex
4- immobilization
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
People with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) often have more than one joint affected by the condition. 
The same two joints on opposite sides of the body are frequently involved with RA. RA impacts 
small joints, which are found in the wrists, hands, and feet.
Isometric exercises are strength-training workouts in which the muscles contract, but the body 
doesn’t move. Isometrics involve tensing a muscle, then relaxing it. This type of training is es­
pecially useful if the usual weight lifting causes your joints to hurt.
- Isometric exercises is the safest type of exercise that patient can do.
Question 19
A 65-year-old patient who suffered a stroke has been referred to rehabilitation with a re­
quest to improve stability. Which therapeutic technique should be selected to improve the 
patient’s stability?
1- Slow reversal hold
2- Rhythmic initiation
3- Placing and holding
4- Alternating isometrics
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
This technique helps to increase strength of weak agonist muscles, active ROM develops co­
ordination by smooth reversible movements helps to reduce fatigue of exercised muscle and 
increase endurance.
Slow  reversal  (SR)  involves  dynamic contraction  of  the antagonist slowly followed by dy­
namic contraction of the agonist. Slow reversal-hold  (SRH)  employs  dynamic  contraction 
followed  by  isometric contraction of the antagonist ,ﬁnally followed by the same contraction 
sequence of the agoinst.
- Rhythmic stabilization is used to improve mobility.
- Placing and holding is used to improve controlled mobility. 
- Alternating isometrics is used to improve skill.

PPTE Review & Study Guide
A 56-year-old man presents to the Physical Therapy clinic after removing a plaster cast, 
which is covering the right knee joint. During the assessment of the right knee joint by a 
physical therapist, a hypo mobility has identified.
Which of the following statements describes the hypo mobility?
1- Joint mobility
2- Joint stiffness
3- Decrease mobility
4- Increase mobility
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
hyopmobility: a decrease in the range of movement of which a body part and especially a joint 
is capable and therefore decrease mobility of joint. Joint stiffness may be identified as amobil­
ity of joint.
Question 21
Which of the following is most effective in mobility in patients with asthma?
1- Hypnotics
2- Beta agonist
3- H2 receptor antagonist
4- Beta adrenergic blockers
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
medications that relax muscles of the airways, causing widening of the airways and resulting in 
easier breathing. H2 receptor antagonist was used for GERD while Beta adrenergic blockers 
were used for heart diseases in the time hypnotics were used for sleep disorders.
Question 22
Which of the following training exercises is defined as overall lengthening of the muscle, 
as it develops tension and contracts to control motion against the resistance of an outside 
force (negative work)?
1- Eccentric
2- Isometric
3- Concentric
4- Open chain
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
eccentric contraction is the motion of an active muscle while it is lengthening under load. Ec­
centric training is repetitively doing eccentric muscle contractions.
Concentric involves muscle shortening while isometric contraction involves no change in mus­
cle length
- Isokinetic involves muscle contraction under fixed velocity.

Therapeutic Modalities - Therapeutic Exercises 
Chapter 5
Type of contraction that make shortening of muscle length:
1- eccentric
2- isometric
3- concentric
4- isokinetic exercise
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Concentric contraction occurs when the total length of the muscle shortens as tension is pro­
duced. Eccentric involve muscle lengthening. Isometric contraction involves no length change 
while isokinetic involves muscle contraction with controlled speed.
Question 24
If the proximal bone of the joint is fixed and the distal part of the limb moves in sequence :
1-  ACL training
2- Closed-chain exercise
3- Open-chain exercise
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
In open kinetic chain exercises, the segment furthest away from the body — known as the 
distal aspect, usually the hand or foot — is free object and not fixed. The opposite happened 
with the closed kinematic chain.
Question 25
Which of the following is most commonly associated with a systematic
exercise plan, planned performance of bodily movements, postures, and
physical activities?
1- Flexibility
2- Endurance
3- Therapeutic
4- Coordination
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Therapeutic exercise involves movement prescribed to correct impairments, restore muscular 
and skeletal function and/or maintain a state of well-being.
It Exercise is a physical activity that is planned and is performed with the goal of attaining or 
maintaining physical fitness. Physical fitness is a set of traits that allows an individual to per­
form physical activity.

PPTE Review & Study Guide
Which of the following is the most appropriate precaution during close kinematic chain 
training?
1- Avoid resistance to the distal tibia.
2- Knees do not move posteriorly to the toes.
3- Avoid extension of knee between 45° to 15°.
4- Avoid strengthening of quadriceps between 60° to 90°.
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
To avoid genu recurvatum and possible Osgood shlutter injury or avulsion fracture.
Question 27
Which of the following is the most appropriate description of the therapeutic exercises for 
timing, sequence and strength of muscles?
1- Mobility
2- Flexibility
3- Endurance
4- Coordination
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Mobility exercise is to maintain ROM.
Flexibility exercise is to improve ROM. 
Endurance exercises is to improve ability of muscle to contract over long period of time. 
Coordination exercises is to improve timing, sequence and strength of muscles.

4- bulk of the soft tissue.

Question 31
During weight bearing, a soft tissue contracture resulting in supination of the forefoot will

1- pronation of the forefoot.

higher in frequency compared to faradic, galvanic and diadynamic which have a frequency of 
50:100 HZ.

tissue structure – essentially, the energy can cause in increase in temperature and a change in 
tissue structure, but that is not the intention with therapy laser which is applied at levels below

2- is a narrow beam that is emitted in a specifi direction.
3-Laser lights are in phase in space and time.
Question 18
In radiating energy when we use it 30 inch from the patient then change it to 15 inch so there

the correct answer is radiating energy will  become 4 times, that’s

of calculation)
      - So to double the distance from an Infrared source decreases the intensity to (1/2)2 = (1/4) 
of its original value.
      - This is true that if there is halving the distance will quadruple the intensity.

Therapeutic Modalities - Electro & Hydro therapy 
Chapter 5
One of the common features of ultrasound is that it produces the greatest rise in tempera­
ture in the skeletal muscles because it is mostly formed by which of the following?
1- Protein
2- Adipose
3- Endothelial cells
4- Connective tissues
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Skeletal muscles contain great amount of protein which known as the best absorber of Ultra­
sound which produces heat so it rise the temperature in the body.
Question 27
Which of the following is the most appropriate characteristic of a beam of therapeutic ultra­
sonic waves from transducer?
 1- Roughly cylindrical
 2- Uniform intensities
 3- More scattered in the far-field
 4- Extreme irregular near the zone
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
There is 10 Important Properties of Ultrasonic Waves:
Property 1: Ultrasonic waves vibrate at a frequency greater than the audible range for humans 
(20 kilohertz).
Property 2: They have smaller wavelengths. As a result, their penetrating power is high.
Property 3: They cannot travel through vacuum.
Property 4: Ultrasonic waves travel at the speed of sound in the medium. They have maximum 
velocity in a denser medium.
Property 5: In a homogeneous medium, they travel at a constant velocity.
Property 6: In low viscosity liquids, ultrasonic waves produce vibrations.
Property 7: They undergo reflection, refraction and absorption.
Property 8: They have high energy content. They can be transmitted over a large distance 
without much loss of energy.
Property 9: They produce intense heat when they are passed through objects.
Property 10:Like sound waves, ultrasonic waves are longitudinal waves that produce alternate 
compressions and rarefactions.

4- Zirconate

rationale:

4- 3 MHz and 0.5 Watts/cm2
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
The correct answer is 1 MHz to reach in deep tissue & 1.5 Watts /cm2 which is an adequate 
intensity for bursitis in hip region , so the choice is 1 MHz and 1.5 Watts/cm2.
Question 38
Which of the following is the most appropriate maximum dosage, in Wcm-2, of Ultrasound 
therapy in chronic inflammatory conditions:
1- 1.0
2- 1.5
3- 2.0
4- 2.5
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
An apparently effective treatment window of pulsed ultrasound, 0.16-0.50 W/cm(2) (SATA), 
proved illusory on closer scrutiny. Conclusions: without a known dose-response relationship 
users of therapeutic ultrasound can only guess at what dosage might be effective for a patient 
and how to modify it. Considerably more clinical research is necessary to justify the dosages 
used in treatment at present.

Therapeutic Modalities - Electro & Hydro therapy 
Chapter 5
33 - year - old patient comes to the Physical Therapy Clinic with chronic lateral elbow pain. 
The physical therapist decides to use ultrasonic therapy for treatment. How is burn prevent­
ed during ultrasonic therapy treatment?
1- Using big head 
2- Using small head
3- moving the head of the ultrasound 
4- Constant the head of the ultrasound
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Ultrasound physical therapy has a low risk of causing complications. But, exposure to low-in­
tensity ultrasound for a long time may cause superficial burns on the skin. So, medical prac­
titioners usually ensure that the ultrasound probe is in motion when in contact with your skin.
Question 40
A patient comes with severe low back pain. After examination, the therapist plans to apply 
Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS). Which of the following is important 
and should be asked about before starting the treatment?
1- Fracture
2- Allergies
3- Hypertension
4- Cardiac pacemaker
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Cardiac pacemaker is the correct answer because it is one of contraindications of TENS be­
cause electrical stimulation could cause electromagnetic interference with pacemakers and 
implanted cardioverter defibrillators.
Question 41
Which of the following theories support the use of a transcutaneous electrical nerve stimu­
lation (TENS) unit for sensory level pain control?
1- Gate control theory
2- Sensory interaction theory
3- Central summation theory
4- None of the above
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
The gate control theory is also thought to be involved when using a TENS machine. The elec­
trical current stimulates nerve fibres that carry signals relating to touch. The signals travel to 
the spinal cord where they temporarily block the transmission of pain sensations to the brain.

358
PPTE Review & Study Guide
TENS stimulation is :
1- Presynaptic inhibition
2- Presynaptic excitation
3- Post synaptic inhibition
4- Post synaptic excitation
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
The correct answer is presynaptic inhibition , TENS unit reduces pain through nociceptive 
inhibition at the presynaptic level in the dorsal horn, thus limiting its central transmission. The 
electrical stimuli on the skin preferentially activate low-threshold, myelinated nerve fibers. The 
afferent input from these fibers inhibits propagation of nociception carried in the small un-my­
elinated C fibers by blocking transmission along these fibers to the target or T cells located in 
the substantia gelatinosa (laminae 2 and 3) of the dorsal horn.
Question 43
When treating chronic pain which type of TENS used:
1- brief
2- conventional
3- burst
4- acupuncture
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
The correct answer is acupuncture like a tens:
     -  In acute stage we use: conventional or high frequency.
     -  In sub-acute stage we use: burst.
     -  In chronic stage we use: low frequency (acupuncture).
Question 44
Patient has chronic brachialgia which is the best TENS use:
1- conventional
2- low frequency
3- burst
4- intense
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
The correct answer is Low frequency , Because:
    - Conventional TENS (low-intensity, high-frequency)
    - Acupuncture-like TENS (high-intensity, low-frequency)
    - Intense TENS (high-intensity, high-frequency)

Therapeutic Modalities - Electro & Hydro therapy 
Chapter 5
Burst tens stimulate:                                                                                                      
1- A delta fiber
2- A beta fiber
3- both of them
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
 Antidromic activation of peripheral nerves by TENS generates nerve impulses that have been 
shown to collide and extinguish afferent impulses arising from peripheral structures. Periph­
eral blockade of nociceptive impulses is more likely when TENS activates A-delta fibres (i.e. 
intense TENS).
Question 46
Patient with elbow pain for 5 months and just stopped playing tennis, which type of TENS 
would you use:
1- Conventional TENS
2- Acupuncture like TENS
3- Brief intense TENS
4- Bust TENS
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
The correct answer is Acupuncture like Tens , described as above, Traditional TENS (Hi TENS) 
Usually use stimulation at a relatively high frequency (90 - 130 Hz The stimulation is delivered 
at ‘normal’ intensity - definitely there but not uncomfortable.
- Acupuncture (Lo) TENS Use a lower frequency stimulation (2-5 Hz) with wider (longer) puls­
es (200-250ms - still not at the patients’ threshold, but quite a definite, strong sensation.
burst TENS interrupting the stimulation outflow at rate of 2 - 3 bursts/second. The stimulation 
intensity will need to be relatively high .
- Extract: Acupuncture TENS is used for any chronic pain
Question 47
What is the best modality to use prior to stretching to prepare the muscle?
1- hot pack
2- cold  aapplication
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Deep heating is thought to lessen nerve sensitivity, increase blood flow, increase tissue metab­
olism, decrease muscle spindle sensitivity to stretch, cause muscle relaxation, and increase 
flexibility.

360
PPTE Review & Study Guide
A 19-year-old man presented to the Physical Therapy Department with severe pain (8 out of 
10 on the pain scale) and swelling in the front of the knee and around the patella. Which of 
the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
1- TENS, rest, ice, compression and exercise
2- Heat, TENS, rest, compression and elevation
3- Heat, exercise, rest, compression and elevation
4- Protection, rest, ice, compression and Elevation
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
RICE treatment is a first-aid treatment for soft tissue injuries like sprains, strains, and bruises 
for example, sprained ankles, sprained knees, or muscle strains. It’s best used immediately 
after sustaining an injury and should be stopped within two days (48 hours).
Question 49
A 75-year-old patient with severe osteoarthritis has been admitted to a nursing home. Which 
of the following is the best modality that the therapist should recommend to assist in reduc­
ing knee pain?
1- Cane
2- Walker
3- Hot modalities, exercises and walking program
4- Cold application, exercises and walking Program
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Hot modalities Provide moist heat to the body which helps in relieving the excess heat. This 
may also assist in relaxing the muscles and loosening up the joints for adequate comfort and 
pain relief, Simple home exercises and stretches can help ease some common types of knee 
pain.
Question 50
What is the best modality to use after muscle soreness?
1- Ice aplication
2- hot pack 
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Ice application or Cold therapy is also known as cryotherapy. It works by reducing blood flow 
to a particular area, which can significantly reduce inflammation and swelling that causes pain, 
especially around a joint or a tendon. It can temporarily reduce nerve activity, which can also 
relieve pain.

Therapeutic Modalities - Electro & Hydro therapy 
Chapter 5
A 19 - year - old man presents to the Physical Therapy clinic after removing a plaster cast, 
which is covering the right elbow joint. The physical therapist decides to start with stretch­
ing exercises to increase the range of motion. Which of the following modalities is used for 
the preparation of stretching?
1- Ice massage
2- Application of local heat
3- High - intensity exercises 
4- Application of cold therapy
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Heat can soothe and heal muscles by increasing blood flow and is more beneficial for chronic 
pain or injuries, Heat is also cited as increasing flexibility and thus reducing the chance of in­
jury, and reducing energy cost of muscle contraction by reducing internal friction.
Question 52
Which of the following is the most appropriate combination of superficial heating modali­
ties?
1- Hot pack, wax bath, hydrotherapy, and infrared
2- Microwave, hot pack, hydrotherapy, and hot water bath
3- Hydrocollator, paraffin wax bar, hydrotherapy, and ultrasound
4- Electric heat pad, fluid therapy diathermy and infrared 
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Moist hot packs are perhaps the most widely used form of superficial heating in the clinical 
setting.
Question 53
When patient coming for you has limited ROM due to edema in addition to leg elevation, you 
can use which type of electrical stimulation:
1- faradic
2- TENS
3- Galvanic
4- didynamic
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
The faradic current increase metabolism and remove waste products and bring more blood 
supply and nutrients to muscle thus increase demand of oxygen and nutrients to the muscle 
so it reduces joints stiffness and increase range of motion.

The tissue of body that consider the best conductor to the electric:                                                                                 
1- nerve      
2- fat
3- muscles
4- bones
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Nerve cells generate electrical signals that transmit information. Although neurons are not 
intrinsically good conductors of electricity, they have evolved elaborate mechanisms for gen­
erating electrical signals based on the flow of ions across their plasma membranes.

Therapeutic Modalities - Electro & Hydro therapy 
Chapter 5
A 35-year-old man fell asleep with his arm on the side of a chair. In the morning, he ob­
served absent sensation on the dorsum of the hand and an inability to extend the wrist. His 
nerve conduction studies and electromyography confirmed neurapraxia of the radial nerve 
in the arm. Which of the following is the most appropriate type of electrotherapy indicated 
for this condition?
 1- Faradic current
 2- Interrupted direct current
 3- Electrical muscle stimulation
 4- Transcutaneous nerve stimulation
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
The electrical impulses can reduce the pain signals going to the spinal cord and brain, which 
may help relieve pain and relax muscles. They may also stimulate the production of endor­
phins, which are the body’s natural painkillers.
Question 72

the shoulder. To administer this treatment using the acetate ion, the current characteristics 
and polarity should be:
1- monophasic twin peaked pulses using the positive pole
2- monophasic twin peaked pulses using the negative pole
3- continuous monophasic using the positive pole
4- continuous monophasic using the negative pole
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
The correct Answer is Continuous monophasic is a direct galvanic current and we using the 
negative pole When we use ionophoresis it must be direct current or continuous monophasic, 
and must put the chemical substance in the same polarity of the electrode, so we choose neg­
ative pole due to the substance is acetate ion.

Tennis elbow player has pain in elbow joint 5 month ago and there is production of pro-in­

Question 75
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
The correct Answer is Pulsed with Lidocain.
NOTE:
Phonophoresis:
1- The use of US to drive medication through the skin into the deeper tissues, Local analgesics 
(lidocaine) and anti-inflammatory drugs {dexamethasone, salicylates) are often used.
2- Method of application is similar to direct contact technique, except tha a medicinal agent is 
used as part of coupling medium:
      - Mode: pulsed 20%
      - Treatment intensity: 1-3 w/cm2.
      - Treatment time: 5-10 minutes.
       - 0.5-0.75 w/cm2, using a medication that is prepared in a medium that will allow transmis
       sion of the US Gel mediums or transdermal patches have good transmissivity; avoid 
       pastes and creams.
3- Goals and indications:
4- pain modulation
      - decreasing inflammation in the subacute and chronic musculoskeletal conditions.
A 58-year-old patient with lower back pain treated by TENS to reduce pain,after the third

adaptation to the intensity and frequency of TENS therapy. Which of the following should

1- Change the treatment agent

rationale:

371
Therapeutic Modalities - Electro & Hydro therapy 
Chapter 5
Which of the following is a consequence of deep heat applied to an impaired arterial supply 
area?
1- Shock
2- Burns
3- Scalds
4- Gangrene
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
The correct answer is Burns, as application of deep heat may cause skin irritation that leads 
to burns.
Question 83
Patient coming with industrial burn involved the dorsum muscle of the left hand after study 
there is dis-continues chronoxia227/m. so we could use:
1- continues direct current
2- faradic current
3- interrupted direct current
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
The correct Answer is continues direct current , due to it`s appear in discontinues chronoxia 
which mean that it`s denervated muscle.
NOTE:
- Rheobase:
1- the smallest current that will produce a muscle contraction if the stimulus is of infinite dura­
tion; in practice an impulse of 1ms (0.1 sec) is used.
2- In denervation, the Rheobase may be less than that of innervated muscle, and it often rises 
as re-innervation commence. These changes are not however sufficiently predictable to be 
reliable guides.
3- The Rheobase varies considerably in different muscles and according to the skin resistance 
and temperature of the part, while a rise may be due to fibrosis of the muscle.
- Chronaxie:
1- The duration of the shortest impulse that will produce a response with a current of double 
the rheobase.
2- The chronaxie of innervated muscle is appreciably than that of denervated muscle, the for­
mer being less and the latter more than 1ms if the constant voltage stimulator is used.
3- With the constant-current stimulator, the values are higher, but bear a similar relationship to 
each other.
4- Chronaxie is not a satisfactory method of testing electrical reactions as partial denervation 
is not clearly shown, the chronaxie being that at the predominant state of the fibers; for exam­
ple, the chronaxie of a muscle with 25% of its fibers innervated would be the same as that of 
a completely denervated muscle.

Question 103
A therapist is treating a patient with a strain at one of the deep muscles and wants to reduce 
pain. Which of the following is the most appropriate form of ultrasound that the therapist 
should use?
1- Pulsed 1 MHz
2- Pulsed 3 MHz
3- Pulsed 5 MHz
4- Non-pulsed 1 MHz
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
More research with various ultrasound machines needs to be performed to see If 3-MHz ultra­
sound is more appropriate than 1-MHz ultrasound for producing thermal effects in tissues 2.5 
cm deep. Researchers can also explore the maximum depth to which 3-MHz ultrasound can 
adequately heat various.
Question 104
A 25-year-old patient comes to the Physical Therapy Clinic with scar tissue at the right leg. 
The physical therapist decides to use ultrasonic therapy for treatment. Which of the follow­
ing occurs for the scar tissue after treatment?
1- Painful
2-Pliable
3- Inflamed
4- Hardness
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
Some collagen breaks down at the site of the wound and the blood supply reduces. The scar 
gradually becomes smoother and softer. Although scars are permanent, they can fade over a 
period of up to 2 years. It’s unlikely they’ll fade any more after this time.

PPTE Review & Study Guide
After applying a hot pack to a patient you observe hyperemia in the treatment area after a 
few minutes. As the therapist you should:
1- remove the hot pack immediately and assess for a burn.
2- keep the hot pack in place as this is indicative of heat dissipation secondary to vasodi­
lation.
3- elevate the part to minimize edema formation.
4- remove the hot pack immediately as the patient is having a potentially dangerous histamine 
reaction.
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
The correct Answer is  keep the hot pack to a patient because it`s the action of the heat to 
make hyperemia due to vasdilation.
Question 106
A 40-year-old woman presented to the physical therapy clinic with hand pain. The physical 
therapist decides to use Paraffin wax for treatment. What happens to the hand after treat­
ment?
 1- Increases in pain
 2- Stiffness of joints
 3- Local hyperemia
 4- Reflex vasoconstriction
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Paraffin wax is a form of deep heat therapy that causes vasodilatation of superficial capillaries 
and arterioles that leads to local hyperemia and reflex vasodilatation.
Question 107
Muscle reeducation In comparing the use of cold pack and hot pack treatments, which of 
the following statements is false?
1- Cold packs penetrate more deeply than hot packs.
2- Cold increases the viscosity of fluid and heat decreases the viscosity of blood.
3- Cold decreases spasm by decreasing sensitivity to muscle spindles and heat decreases 
spasm by decreasing nerve conduction velocity.
4- Cold decreases the rate of oxygen uptake, and heat increases the rate of oxygen uptake.
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Cold decreases spasm by decreasing sensitivity to muscle spindles and heat decrease spasm 
by decreasing nerve conduction velocity, cold: decrease spasm by decrease muscle tension 
by increasing in the threshold of activation of the muscle spindle Decreased muscle spasm, 
the muscle relaxation probably results from a decrease in firing rates of the efferent fibers in 
the muscle spindle.

Therapeutic Modalities - Electro & Hydro therapy 
Chapter 5
A patient recently diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis presents to a physical therapy clinic. 
The patient asks the therapist what she needs to avoid with this condition. Which of the 
following should the patient avoid?
1- Hot tubs
2- Slightly increased intake of fluids
3- Application of ice packs
4- Strength training
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
The correct Answer is Hot Tubs , any hot application is avoided for multiple sclerosis.
Question 109
A 58-year-old woman presented with severe hip pain. She has been taking steroids for her 
dermatomyositis. A CT scan hip confirmed avascular necrosis of femoral neck with an im­
pacted fracture. There is a 2 cm leg-length discrepancy. Which of the following is the most 
appropriate intervention to reduce hip pain?
1- Shoe raise
2- Walking stick
3- Shortwave diathermy
4- Modified seating system 
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
Diathermy are treatments that deliver energy to treat specific areas of the body. These treat­
ments are typically used for the following purposes: Relieve pain, stiffness and muscle spasms. 
Reduce joint contractures.
Question 110
Use of shortwave diathermy and microwave diathermy is not contraindicated in which of 
the following conditions?
1- On a patient who has a pacemaker.
2- Over the site of a metal implant.
3- On a patient who has hemophilia.
4- Using pulse shortwave over an acute injury.
Correct Answer: 4
rationale:
Shortwave diathermy has the following precautions or contraindicatios:
1- Malignancy                                                          2- Sensory loss
3- Tuberculosis                                                        4- pregnancy
5- Metallic implants or foreign bodies.
6- Application over moist dressings.
7- Ischemic areas or arteriosclerosis.
8- Thromboangiitis obliterans.

of gases at low pressure. A high potential of several thousand volts applied to the electrodes 
ionizes the gas in the tube, causing it to emit colored light. The color of the light depends on

Question 123

rationale:

patients and device are 45 to 75cm. The wavelength is 800 nm and perpendicular to the area 
of pain. The process of therapy takes time between 10 and 15 minutes and can be done re­

liquid.

Therapeutic Modalities - Electro & Hydro therapy 
Chapter 5
A therapist should consider using a form of treatment other than moist heat application on the 
posterior lumbar region of all of the following patients except:
1- Patient with a history of hemophilia
2- Patient with a history of malignant cancer under the site of heat application.
3- Patient with a history of Raynaud’s phenomenon
4- Patient with a history including many years of
Correct Answer: 3
rationale:
The correct answer is patient with a history of Raynaud’s phenomenon, 
Warm water soaks- Research has found that for individuals with Raynaud’s, soaking your 
hands in hot water for five minutes every four hours increased blood flow for at least 2 hours 
and decreases the number and occurrence attacks.
Question 147
Apist routinely places ice on the ankle of a patient with an acute ankle sprain. Ice applica­
tion has many therapeutic benefits. Which of the following is the body’s first response to 
application of ice?
1- Vasoconstriction of local vessels
2- Decreased nerve conduction velocity
3- Decreased local sensitivity
4- All occur simultaneously
Correct Answer: 1
rationale:
Normally, the vessels that supply blood to the skin constrict or narrow in response to cold 
temperatures. This reaction, called “vasoconstriction,” decreases blood flow to the skin, which 
helps to minimize heat loss from the warm blood and therefore preserve a normal internal or 
“core” .
Question 148
Tool provide physiotherapist with visual and auditory signals to monitor muscle recovery?
1- Biofeedback
2- EMG
Correct Answer: 2
rationale:
The correct answer is EMG ELectromyography (EMG) is a diagnostic procedure to assess 
the health of muscles and the nerve cells that control them (motor neurons). EMG results can 
reveal nerve dysfunction, muscle dysfunction or problems with nerve-to-muscle signal trans­
mission.
